answer: An agent economy can require every identity to escrow a stake before it may vote, receive jobs, or collect fees. At random, peers issue the same task to several identities and compare signed answers; if identities collude or contradict one another, a verification contract slashes their bonds. A Sybil attacker therefore must lock fresh capital for each mask, while risking loss when quill, ember, and lantern agents expose correlated behavior, making mass identities economically expensive.
